mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) indicates inflationary pressure, which typically leads to monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the inflation signal, or CPIAUCSL increases are not followed by Fed rate hikes.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals a tightening labor market, which historically correlates with increased corporate earnings and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the labor market signal, or UNRATE drops below 5% are not followed by earnings growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 50% of instances despite the demand signal, or RSAFS increases are not followed by revenue growth.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in Industrial Production (INDPRO) signals a slowdown in economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the slowdown signal, or INDPRO declines are not followed by GDP contraction.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) rises by more than 0.5% in a month, the combination signals a potential inflationary surge not yet addressed by monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the inflation and low-rate signal, or the Fed raises rates within the next 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 7% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) declines for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 7% and PAYEMS declines for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the labor market signal, or the labor market indicators do not lead to GDP contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) coupled with a rise in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) indicates a robust demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises > 5% and RSAFS rises > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the demand signal, or the demand indicators do not lead to GDP growth.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, a decline in Industrial Production (INDPRO) coupled with a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals an impending economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines > 0.5% and UNRATE rises > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the slowdown signal, or the economic indicators do not lead to a broader market downturn.
